This is NOT verified legal compliance and NOT a substitute for review by qualified Polish legal counsel. Scope: National("PL") — this file covers ONLY Poland-specific law that supplements the EU-wide baseline already covered in national/eu.json (GDPR, DSA, UCPD, EU AI Act) — it does not duplicate that content. Every rule's action is a conservative, generic engineering policy, not a legal conclusion. This content will age — re-verify before relying on it. Enriched 2026-10-27 with additional rules from live web search results (sherloc.unodc.org, hatecrime.osce.org, fra.europa.eu, law-firm summaries); existing rules unchanged; added rules are Log only and several rest on secondary summaries — re-verify against Dziennik Ustaw.

rules.source: Polish Act of 10 May 2018 on the Protection of Personal Data — fixes the national age of digital consent (GDPR Article 8) at 16, matching the GDPR default rather than lowering it; establishes UODO (Urząd Ochrony Danych Osobowych) as the supervisory authority. https://www.recordinglaw.com/world-laws/world-data-privacy-laws/poland-data-privacy-laws/

Poland's August 2024 implementation of Directive (EU) 2020/1828 on representative actions — allows authorized consumer organizations to bring collective actions on behalf of consumers, including for GDPR violations; UOKiK (Office of Competition and Consumer Protection) separately enforces unfair market practices and is developing tooling to detect dark patterns in online commerce. https://www.dataguidance.com/jurisdiction/poland

Act on Artificial Intelligence Systems (Ustawa o systemach sztucznej inteligencji) — adopted by Parliament 3 July 2026, signed by the President 24 July 2026, published in the 2026 Journal of Laws 27 July 2026, in force 11 August 2026 — https://www.regulatoryai.eu/ai-act-poland/
rules.retrieved_snippet: National implementing legislation for the EU AI Act — genuinely national-specific, not a restatement of eu.json's AI Act rules: creates the Commission for the Development and Safety of AI (KRiBSI), nested within the Ministry of Digital Affairs, as Poland's single market-surveillance authority (one of only two EU states, with Lithuania, to designate a sole authority), with real inspection, sanction, and regulatory-sandbox powers. From 2 August 2026, businesses in Poland must also comply with EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations (chatbots, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, deepfakes).

rules.source: Act on ensuring compliance with digital accessibility requirements (implementing the European Accessibility Act) — entered into force June 2025; earlier Act on Digital Accessibility of Websites and Mobile Applications of Public Entities of 4 April 2019 (transposing the EU Web Accessibility Directive) — https://www.w3.org/WAI/policies/poland/
rules.retrieved_snippet: The 2019 Act requires Polish public-sector websites/apps to meet WCAG 2.1 AA and publish an accessibility statement, with fines from PLN 5,000 to 100,000. The 2025 EAA-implementing Act extends WCAG 2.1 AA obligations to many private-sector companies as well, effective 28 June 2025 — genuinely broader than the EU-wide baseline and not yet covered in eu.json.

rules.source: Criminal Code Article 267 (unauthorised acquisition of information) — UNODC SHERLOC English translation https://sherloc.unodc.org/cld/en/legislation/pol/penal_code/chapter_xxxiii/article_267/article_267.html
rules.retrieved_snippet: UNODC translation: § 1 covers acquiring information not meant for the offender by opening sealed mail, tapping a communications line or breaking electronic protection, punishable by a fine, restriction of liberty or imprisonment up to 2 years; § 2 extends to installing or using interception equipment; a Polish-language version also lists a separate paragraph on unauthorised access to an IT system, so numbering differs between sources.

rules.source: Act on the National Cybersecurity System (KSC) as amended to implement NIS2 — Clifford Chance https://www.cliffordchance.com/briefings/2026/03/poland--delayed-implementation-of-the-nis2-directive-.html
rules.retrieved_snippet: Law-firm briefings: the President signed the NIS2-implementing amendment on 19 February 2026 and it took effect in early April 2026, introducing self-identification for entities in 18 sectors; the President referred parts (high-risk providers, security orders, administrative penalties) to the Constitutional Tribunal, so provisions may change. Secondary source; check the Journal of Laws.

rules.source: Criminal Code Articles 256 and 257 — OSCE ODIHR hate-crime database https://hatecrime.osce.org/node/1775
rules.retrieved_snippet: Summaries: Article 256 covers promoting a fascist or other totalitarian system or inciting hatred on national, ethnic, racial or religious grounds; Article 257 covers public insult of a group or person on such grounds; sources disagree on the Article 257 maximum penalty (two vs three years) and a 2024 amendment adding further protected grounds was reported but its status was not confirmed.

rules.source: Act on Counteracting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 1 March 2018 (GIIF) — https://www.elliptic.co/country-guides/poland
rules.retrieved_snippet: Secondary guides: the 2018 Act transposes the EU AML directives, lists obligated entities, and treats virtual-currency/crypto-asset service providers as obliged institutions requiring registration; a March 2026 bill (No. 2363) to align AML provisions with Regulation 2023/1114/EU was reported at the Sejm (enactment not confirmed). Not an official source.
